Lemma
[Dependence of hypersurface geometry on the ambient metric] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0294, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0295, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0296 1. ch34:34.19\group Hyperbolic Almost Isometries

Let $N^{n-1}\subset M^n$ be an oriented smooth hypersurface, and let $ u $ and $\widetilde u $ be the same-side unit normals for metrics $g$ and $\widetilde g$. Uniformly on a fixed coordinate neighborhood, egin{align*} |\widetilde u - u |_g& \le C\| \widetilde g-g\| _{C^0},\ |\widetilde abla \widetilde u |_g& \le C, & | abla (\widetilde u - u )|_g& \le C\| \widetilde g-g\| _{C^1},\ |\widetilde{\mathrm{II}}(X,Y)-\mathrm{II}(X,Y)| & \le C|X|_g|Y|_g\| \widetilde g-g\| _{C^1},\ |\widetilde abla \widetilde{\mathrm{II}}(X,Y)- abla \mathrm{II}(X,Y)| & \le C|X|_g|Y|_g\| \widetilde g-g\| _{C^2}. \end{align*}
Proof

\sketch Choose adapted coordinates with $N=\{ x^n=0\} $. Solving the orthogonality equations expresses the unnormalized normal rationally in the metric coefficients and the inverse tangential metric; normalization then proves the first estimate, and differentiation proves the second pair. The identity $\mathrm{II}(X,Y)=g( abla _X u ,Y)$, together with $|(\widetilde abla - abla )Y|_g\le C|Y|_g\| \widetilde g-g\| _{C^1}$, gives the third estimate. Differentiating this identity once more gives the last.

□
